tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert a DXF drawing into G-code for a pen plotter built on an Ender 3 V3 SE.

The pen replaces the hotend. "Pen up / pen down" is done with the Z axis, so no
servo or extra hardware is needed. No heaters are turned on and nothing extrudes.

Usage:
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf                 # writes drawing.gcode
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf -o out.gcode --fit --center

Run with --help for all options. See README.md for pen setup.
"""
import argparse
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import ezdxf
    from ezdxf import disassemble
    from ezdxf.path import make_path
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Missing dependency. Install it with:  pip install ezdxf")

# $INSUNITS code -> millimetres per drawing unit
UNIT_TO_MM = {0: 1.0, 1: 25.4, 2: 304.8, 4: 1.0, 5: 10.0, 6: 1000.0, 8: 0.0254}

# Ender 3 V3 SE bed is 220 x 220 mm.
BED = 220.0


def collect_polylines(msp, flatten_dist):
    """Return a list of polylines ([(x, y), ...], is_closed) in drawing units.

    recursive_decompose explodes INSERT (blocks), hatches' edges, dimensions, etc.
    into plain primitives; make_path + flattening turns arcs, circles, ellipses,
    splines and polylines (incl. bulges) into straight segments.
    """
    out = []
    for e in disassemble.recursive_decompose(msp):
        try:
            path = make_path(e)
        except TypeError:
            continue  # TEXT, POINT, etc. - not drawable as strokes
        for sub in path.sub_paths():
            pts = [(v.x, v.y) for v in sub.flattening(flatten_dist)]
            if len(pts) >= 2:
                closed = math.dist(pts[0], pts[-1]) < 1e-6
                out.append((pts, closed))
    return out


def bounds(polys):
    xs = [p[0] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    ys = [p[1] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    return min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys)


def transform(polys, scale, dx, dy):
    return [([(x * scale + dx, y * scale + dy) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]


def order_polylines(polys, start=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """Greedy nearest-neighbour ordering to cut pen-up travel. Open paths may be
    reversed; closed paths are left alone (the pen just starts at one end)."""
    remaining = list(polys)
    ordered = []
    cur = start
    while remaining:
        best_i, best_d, best_rev = 0, float("inf"), False
        for i, (pl, closed) in enumerate(remaining):
            d = math.dist(cur, pl[0])
            if d < best_d:
                best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, False
            if not closed:
                d = math.dist(cur, pl[-1])
                if d < best_d:
                    best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, True
        pl, closed = remaining.pop(best_i)
        if best_rev:
            pl = pl[::-1]
        ordered.append((pl, closed))
        cur = pl[-1]
    return ordered


def write_gcode(polys, args, out):
    w = out.write
    w("; Pen plotter G-code generated by dxf_to_gcode.py\n")
    w(f"; pen up Z={args.z_up}  pen down Z={args.z_down}  draw F={args.draw_speed}  travel F={args.travel_speed}\n")
    w("G21 ; millimetres\n")
    w("G90 ; absolute positioning\n")
    w("M104 S0 ; hotend off\n")
    w("M140 S0 ; bed off\n")
    if args.home_z:
        w("G28 ; home all axes (Z uses the probe, so the bed centre is probed)\n")
    else:
        w("G28 X Y ; home X/Y only\n")
        w(f"G92 Z{args.z_up} ; ASSUMES the pen was manually lowered/raised to the pen-up height before starting\n")
    w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed} ; pen up\n")
    if args.pause_for_paper:
        w(f"G0 X{args.paper_x:.2f} Y{args.paper_y:.2f} F{args.travel_speed}\n")
        w("M0 Load paper / check pen, then click to start\n")

    pen_down = False
    pos = None
    for pl, closed in polys:
        x0, y0 = pl[0]
        if pos is None or math.dist(pos, (x0, y0)) > args.join_tol:
            if pen_down:
                w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed}\n")
                pen_down = False
            w(f"G0 X{x0:.3f} Y{y0:.3f} F{args.travel_speed}\n")
        if not pen_down:
            w(f"G1 Z{args.z_down} F{args.z_speed}\n")
            pen_down = True
            w(f"F{args.draw_speed}\n")
        for x, y in pl[1:]:
            w(f"G1 X{x:.3f} Y{y:.3f}\n")
        pos = pl[-1]

    w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed} ; pen up\n")
    w(f"G0 X0 Y{BED - 20:.0f} F{args.travel_speed} ; park out of the way\n")
    w("M84 ; motors off\n")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("dxf")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="output .gcode (default: next to the DXF)")
    ap.add_argument("--units", choices=["auto", "mm", "cm", "in", "ft", "m"], default="auto",
                    help="DXF drawing units. auto = read from file, assume mm if unset")
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=1.0, help="extra scale factor (default 1)")
    ap.add_argument("--fit", action="store_true", help="scale down (never up) to fit the drawing area")
    ap.add_argument("--center", action="store_true", help="centre the drawing in the drawing area")
    ap.add_argument("--origin-x", type=float, default=10.0, help="drawing area left edge, mm (default 10)")
    ap.add_argument("--origin-y", type=float, default=10.0, help="drawing area front edge, mm (default 10)")
    ap.add_argument("--area-w", type=float, default=200.0, help="drawing area width, mm (default 200)")
    ap.add_argument("--area-h", type=float, default=200.0, help="drawing area height, mm (default 200)")
    ap.add_argument("--z-up", type=float, default=5.0, help="Z with pen lifted (default 5)")
    ap.add_argument("--z-down", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="Z with pen touching paper (default 0; tune by a fraction of a mm, negative = press harder)")
    ap.add_argument("--draw-speed", type=int, default=2000, help="drawing feedrate mm/min (default 2000)")
    ap.add_argument("--travel-speed", type=int, default=6000, help="pen-up feedrate mm/min (default 6000)")
    ap.add_argument("--z-speed", type=int, default=600, help="Z feedrate mm/min (default 600)")
    ap.add_argument("--flatten", type=float, default=0.05,
                    help="max curve error in mm when approximating arcs/splines (default 0.05)")
    ap.add_argument("--join-tol", type=float, default=0.05,
                    help="don't lift the pen if the next stroke starts within this many mm (default 0.05)")
    ap.add_argument("--home-z", action="store_true",
                    help="use full G28 (probes Z at bed centre). Default homes XY only and sets Z by hand")
    ap.add_argument("--pause-for-paper", action="store_true", help="insert an M0 pause before drawing")
    ap.add_argument("--paper-x", type=float, default=110.0)
    ap.add_argument("--paper-y", type=float, default=110.0)
    ap.add_argument("--flip-y", action="store_true", help="mirror Y (if your drawing comes out upside-down)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    doc = ezdxf.readfile(args.dxf)
    if args.units == "auto":
        mm_per_unit = UNIT_TO_MM.get(doc.header.get("$INSUNITS", 0), 1.0)
    else:
        mm_per_unit = {"mm": 1.0, "cm": 10.0, "in": 25.4, "ft": 304.8, "m": 1000.0}[args.units]

    polys = collect_polylines(doc.modelspace(), args.flatten / mm_per_unit)
    if not polys:
        sys.exit("No drawable geometry found in the DXF (text and points are skipped).")

    if args.flip_y:
        polys = [([(x, -y) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]

    scale = mm_per_unit * args.scale
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = bounds(polys)
    w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    if args.fit and (w > args.area_w or h > args.area_h):
        scale *= min(args.area_w / w, args.area_h / h)
        w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    ox = args.origin_x + ((args.area_w - w) / 2 if args.center else 0)
    oy = args.origin_y + ((args.area_h - h) / 2 if args.center else 0)
    polys = transform(polys, scale, ox - minx * scale, oy - miny * scale)

    fx0, fy0, fx1, fy1 = bounds(polys)
    if fx0 < 0 or fy0 < 0 or fx1 > BED or fy1 > BED:
        sys.exit(f"Drawing ({fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm) does not fit the {BED:.0f} mm bed. "
                 "Use --fit or --scale.")

    polys = order_polylines(polys)
    out_path = Path(args.output) if args.output else Path(args.dxf).with_suffix(".gcode")
    with open(out_path, "w", newline="\n") as f:
        write_gcode(polys, args, f)

    print(f"Wrote {out_path}: {len(polys)} strokes, drawing {fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm "
          f"at X{fx0:.1f}-{fx1:.1f} Y{fy0:.1f}-{fy1:.1f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

servo or extra hardware is needed. No heaters are turned on and nothing extrudes.

Usage:
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf                 # writes drawing.gcode
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf -o out.gcode --fit --center

Run with --help for all options. See README.md for pen setup.
"""
import argparse
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import ezdxf
    from ezdxf import disassemble
    from ezdxf.path import make_path
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Missing dependency. Install it with:  pip install ezdxf")

# $INSUNITS code -> millimetres per drawing unit
UNIT_TO_MM = {0: 1.0, 1: 25.4, 2: 304.8, 4: 1.0, 5: 10.0, 6: 1000.0, 8: 0.0254}

# Ender 3 V3 SE bed is 220 x 220 mm.
BED = 220.0


def collect_polylines(msp, flatten_dist):
    """Return a list of polylines ([(x, y), ...], is_closed) in drawing units.

    recursive_decompose explodes INSERT (blocks), hatches' edges, dimensions, etc.
    into plain primitives; make_path + flattening turns arcs, circles, ellipses,
    splines and polylines (incl. bulges) into straight segments.
    """
    out = []
    for e in disassemble.recursive_decompose(msp):
        try:
            path = make_path(e)
        except TypeError:
            continue  # TEXT, POINT, etc. - not drawable as strokes
        for sub in path.sub_paths():
            pts = [(v.x, v.y) for v in sub.flattening(flatten_dist)]
            if len(pts) >= 2:
                closed = math.dist(pts[0], pts[-1]) < 1e-6
                out.append((pts, closed))
    return out


def bounds(polys):
    xs = [p[0] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    ys = [p[1] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    return min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys)


def transform(polys, scale, dx, dy):
    return [([(x * scale + dx, y * scale + dy) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]


def order_polylines(polys, start=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """Greedy nearest-neighbour ordering to cut pen-up travel. Open paths may be
    reversed; closed paths are left alone (the pen just starts at one end)."""
    remaining = list(polys)
    ordered = []
    cur = start
    while remaining:
        best_i, best_d, best_rev = 0, float("inf"), False
        for i, (pl, closed) in enumerate(remaining):
            d = math.dist(cur, pl[0])
            if d < best_d:
                best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, False
            if not closed:
                d = math.dist(cur, pl[-1])
                if d < best_d:
                    best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, True
        pl, closed = remaining.pop(best_i)
        if best_rev:
            pl = pl[::-1]
        ordered.append((pl, closed))
        cur = pl[-1]
    return ordered

    w = out.write
    w("; Pen plotter G-code generated by dxf_to_gcode.py\n")
    w(f"; pen up Z={args.z_up}  pen down Z={args.z_down}  draw F={args.draw_speed}  travel F={args.travel_speed}\n")
    w("G21 ; millimetres\n")
    w("G90 ; absolute positioning\n")
    w("M104 S0 ; hotend off\n")
    w("M140 S0 ; bed off\n")
    if args.home_z:
        w("G28 ; home all axes (Z uses the probe, so the bed centre is probed)\n")
    else:
        w("G28 X Y ; home X/Y only\n")
        w(f"G92 Z{args.z_up} ; ASSUMES the pen was manually lowered/raised to the pen-up height before starting\n")
    w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed} ; pen up\n")
    if args.pause_for_paper:

    ap.add_argument("--z-down", type=float, default=0.0,

    ap.add_argument("--draw-speed", type=int, default=2000, help="drawing feedrate mm/min (default 2000)")

    ap.add_argument("--flatten", type=float, default=0.05,

    ap.add_argument("--join-tol", type=float, default=0.05,

    w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    if args.fit and (w > args.area_w or h > args.area_h):

        write_gcode(polys, args, f)

    print(f"Wrote {out_path}: {len(polys)} strokes, drawing {fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm "
          f"at X{fx0:.1f}-{fx1:.1f} Y{fy0:.1f}-{fy1:.1f}")

   values press harder. Or pass `--home-z` to use a normal `G28` instead.
4. Tape the paper down. The default drawing area is X/Y 10–210 mm of the 220 mm bed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert a DXF drawing into G-code for a pen plotter built on an Ender 3 V3 SE.

The pen replaces the hotend. "Pen up / pen down" is done with the Z axis, so no
servo or extra hardware is needed. No heaters are turned on and nothing extrudes.

Usage:
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf                 # writes drawing.gcode
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf -o out.gcode --fit --center

Run with --help for all options. See README.md for pen setup.
"""
import argparse
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import ezdxf
    from ezdxf import disassemble
    from ezdxf.path import make_path
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Missing dependency. Install it with:  pip install ezdxf")

# $INSUNITS code -> millimetres per drawing unit
UNIT_TO_MM = {0: 1.0, 1: 25.4, 2: 304.8, 4: 1.0, 5: 10.0, 6: 1000.0, 8: 0.0254}

# Ender 3 V3 SE bed is 220 x 220 mm.
BED = 220.0


def collect_polylines(msp, flatten_dist):
    """Return a list of polylines ([(x, y), ...], is_closed) in drawing units.

    recursive_decompose explodes INSERT (blocks), hatches' edges, dimensions, etc.
    into plain primitives; make_path + flattening turns arcs, circles, ellipses,
    splines and polylines (incl. bulges) into straight segments.
    """
    out = []
    for e in disassemble.recursive_decompose(msp):
        try:
            path = make_path(e)
        except TypeError:
            continue  # TEXT, POINT, etc. - not drawable as strokes
        for sub in path.sub_paths():
            pts = [(v.x, v.y) for v in sub.flattening(flatten_dist)]
            if len(pts) >= 2:
                closed = math.dist(pts[0], pts[-1]) < 1e-6
                out.append((pts, closed))
    return out


def bounds(polys):
    xs = [p[0] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    ys = [p[1] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    return min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys)


def transform(polys, scale, dx, dy):
    return [([(x * scale + dx, y * scale + dy) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]


def order_polylines(polys, start=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """Greedy nearest-neighbour ordering to cut pen-up travel. Open paths may be
    reversed; closed paths are left alone (the pen just starts at one end)."""
    remaining = list(polys)
    ordered = []
    cur = start
    while remaining:
        best_i, best_d, best_rev = 0, float("inf"), False
        for i, (pl, closed) in enumerate(remaining):
            d = math.dist(cur, pl[0])
            if d < best_d:
                best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, False
            if not closed:
                d = math.dist(cur, pl[-1])
                if d < best_d:
                    best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, True
        pl, closed = remaining.pop(best_i)
        if best_rev:
            pl = pl[::-1]
        ordered.append((pl, closed))
        cur = pl[-1]
    return ordered


def write_gcode(polys, args, out):
    w = out.write
    w("; Pen plotter G-code generated by dxf_to_gcode.py\n")
    w(f"; pen up Z={args.z_up}  pen down Z={args.z_down}  draw F={args.draw_speed}  travel F={args.travel_speed}\n")
    w("G21 ; millimetres\n")
    w("G90 ; absolute positioning\n")
    w("M104 S0 ; hotend off\n")
    w("M140 S0 ; bed off\n")
    if args.home_z:
        w("G28 ; home all axes (Z uses the probe, so the bed centre is probed)\n")
    else:
        w("G28 X Y ; home X/Y only\n")
        w("M211 S0 ; software endstops off so Z can go below the assumed start height
")
        w(f"G92 Z{args.z_up} ; ASSUMES the pen was manually lowered/raised to the pen-up height before starting\n")
    w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed} ; pen up\n")
    if args.pause_for_paper:
        w(f"G0 X{args.paper_x:.2f} Y{args.paper_y:.2f} F{args.travel_speed}\n")
        w("M0 Load paper / check pen, then click to start\n")

    pen_down = False
    pos = None
    for pl, closed in polys:
        x0, y0 = pl[0]
        if pos is None or math.dist(pos, (x0, y0)) > args.join_tol:
            if pen_down:
                w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed}\n")
                pen_down = False
            w(f"G0 X{x0:.3f} Y{y0:.3f} F{args.travel_speed}\n")
        if not pen_down:
            w(f"G1 Z{args.z_down} F{args.z_speed}\n")
            pen_down = True
            w(f"F{args.draw_speed}\n")
        for x, y in pl[1:]:
            w(f"G1 X{x:.3f} Y{y:.3f}\n")
        pos = pl[-1]

    w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed} ; pen up\n")
    w(f"G0 X0 Y{BED - 20:.0f} F{args.travel_speed} ; park out of the way\n")
    w("M84 ; motors off\n")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("dxf")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="output .gcode (default: next to the DXF)")
    ap.add_argument("--units", choices=["auto", "mm", "cm", "in", "ft", "m"], default="auto",
                    help="DXF drawing units. auto = read from file, assume mm if unset")
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=1.0, help="extra scale factor (default 1)")
    ap.add_argument("--fit", action="store_true", help="scale down (never up) to fit the drawing area")
    ap.add_argument("--center", action="store_true", help="centre the drawing in the drawing area")
    ap.add_argument("--origin-x", type=float, default=10.0, help="drawing area left edge, mm (default 10)")
    ap.add_argument("--origin-y", type=float, default=10.0, help="drawing area front edge, mm (default 10)")
    ap.add_argument("--area-w", type=float, default=200.0, help="drawing area width, mm (default 200)")
    ap.add_argument("--area-h", type=float, default=200.0, help="drawing area height, mm (default 200)")
    ap.add_argument("--z-up", type=float, default=5.0, help="Z with pen lifted (default 5)")
    ap.add_argument("--z-down", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="Z with pen touching paper (default 0; tune by a fraction of a mm, negative = press harder)")
    ap.add_argument("--draw-speed", type=int, default=2000, help="drawing feedrate mm/min (default 2000)")
    ap.add_argument("--travel-speed", type=int, default=6000, help="pen-up feedrate mm/min (default 6000)")
    ap.add_argument("--z-speed", type=int, default=600, help="Z feedrate mm/min (default 600)")
    ap.add_argument("--flatten", type=float, default=0.05,
                    help="max curve error in mm when approximating arcs/splines (default 0.05)")
    ap.add_argument("--join-tol", type=float, default=0.05,
                    help="don't lift the pen if the next stroke starts within this many mm (default 0.05)")
    ap.add_argument("--home-z", action="store_true",
                    help="use full G28 (probes Z at bed centre). Default homes XY only and sets Z by hand")
    ap.add_argument("--pause-for-paper", action="store_true", help="insert an M0 pause before drawing")
    ap.add_argument("--paper-x", type=float, default=110.0)
    ap.add_argument("--paper-y", type=float, default=110.0)
    ap.add_argument("--flip-y", action="store_true", help="mirror Y (if your drawing comes out upside-down)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    doc = ezdxf.readfile(args.dxf)
    if args.units == "auto":
        mm_per_unit = UNIT_TO_MM.get(doc.header.get("$INSUNITS", 0), 1.0)
    else:
        mm_per_unit = {"mm": 1.0, "cm": 10.0, "in": 25.4, "ft": 304.8, "m": 1000.0}[args.units]

    polys = collect_polylines(doc.modelspace(), args.flatten / mm_per_unit)
    if not polys:
        sys.exit("No drawable geometry found in the DXF (text and points are skipped).")

    if args.flip_y:
        polys = [([(x, -y) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]

    scale = mm_per_unit * args.scale
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = bounds(polys)
    w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    if args.fit and (w > args.area_w or h > args.area_h):
        scale *= min(args.area_w / w, args.area_h / h)
        w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    ox = args.origin_x + ((args.area_w - w) / 2 if args.center else 0)
    oy = args.origin_y + ((args.area_h - h) / 2 if args.center else 0)
    polys = transform(polys, scale, ox - minx * scale, oy - miny * scale)

    fx0, fy0, fx1, fy1 = bounds(polys)
    if fx0 < 0 or fy0 < 0 or fx1 > BED or fy1 > BED:
        sys.exit(f"Drawing ({fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm) does not fit the {BED:.0f} mm bed. "
                 "Use --fit or --scale.")

    polys = order_polylines(polys)
    out_path = Path(args.output) if args.output else Path(args.dxf).with_suffix(".gcode")
    with open(out_path, "w", newline="\n") as f:
        write_gcode(polys, args, f)

    print(f"Wrote {out_path}: {len(polys)} strokes, drawing {fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm "
          f"at X{fx0:.1f}-{fx1:.1f} Y{fy0:.1f}-{fy1:.1f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
I wrote the converter and merged it to `main` (PR #12). It's at `scripts/dxf-to-gcode/dxf_to_gcode.py`, with a README next to it. I only tested it on a sample DXF I made (a line, circle, arc, closed polyline and spline), not on your printer. The output looked right: the header, the strokes, the drawing landing inside the bed, and the park move at the end.

**Using it**
```bash
pip install ezdxf
python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf --fit --center
```
This writes `drawing.gcode` next to the DXF. Copy it to the SD card and print it.

**What it handles**
- It draws lines, arcs, circles, ellipses, splines, polylines and blocks.
- It skips text and points. To draw text, convert it to curves in your CAD program first.
- It draws everything with one pen and ignores layers and colors.
- It reorders the strokes so the pen travels less between them.
- `--fit` shrinks a drawing that's too big for the paper area but never enlarges it. `--center` centers it. `--flip-y` is there in case your drawing comes out upside-down.
- It reads the DXF's units automatically. If that's wrong, use `--units`.

**Before your first run**
- The pen goes up and down using the Z axis, and the heaters stay off.
- By default the script homes only X and Y. The V3 SE normally finds Z height with its probe, which doesn't suit a pen.
- Before you start, use the printer's menu to raise the pen about 5 mm above the paper.
- The script then lowers the pen 5 mm to draw. Adjust `--z-down` until the pen just touches the paper; a negative value presses harder. Start with a tiny change, like -0.2.
- If you'd rather use the normal probe homing, pass `--home-z`.
- The default drawing area is 200 × 200 mm, inset 10 mm from the bed edges. Change it with the `--origin-*` and `--area-*` options.

Run a small drawing first with the pen barely touching, so a wrong Z setting doesn't push the pen into the bed.

content.text:
Copy the **`.gcode` file** the script produces, and nothing else. For example, if you ran it on `drawing.dxf`, copy `drawing.gcode`. It's saved in the same folder as your DXF unless you used `-o` to put it elsewhere.

You don't need the DXF or the Python script on the SD card.

Tips:
- Use a FAT32-formatted card. The printer's own card works fine.
- Keep the file name short, with no unusual characters. Letters, numbers and underscores are safest.
- Eject the card from your computer properly before you put it in the printer. Then pick the file from the printer's menu.

content.text:
After the install finishes, you run the script. Here are the steps:

1. **Open a terminal in the script's folder.** In File Explorer, go to `HELP-ME\scripts\dxf-to-gcode`, click the address bar, type `cmd` and press Enter.

2. **Put your DXF in that folder**, or use its full path in the next step.

3. **Run the script**, replacing `drawing.dxf` with your file's name:
   ```bash
   python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf --fit --center
   ```
   It prints a line like `Wrote drawing.gcode: 5 strokes, drawing 100.0 x 95.0 mm`. That means it worked.

4. **Copy `drawing.gcode`** to the SD card, put the card in the printer, and pick the file from the menu.

5. **Before you start the print:**
   - Tape the paper to the bed.
   - Raise the pen about 5 mm above the paper using the printer's menu (Move → Z).
   - Start the print, and watch the first few strokes. If the pen doesn't touch the paper, adjust `--z-down` and generate the file again.

If step 3 prints an error, paste it here and I'll fix it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert a DXF drawing into G-code for a pen plotter built on an Ender 3 V3 SE.

The pen replaces the hotend. "Pen up / pen down" is done with the Z axis, so no
servo or extra hardware is needed. No heaters are turned on and nothing extrudes.

Usage:
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf                 # writes drawing.gcode
    python dxf_to_gcode.py drawing.dxf -o out.gcode --fit --center

Run with --help for all options. See README.md for pen setup.
"""
import argparse
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import ezdxf
    from ezdxf import disassemble
    from ezdxf.path import make_path
except ImportError:
    sys.exit("Missing dependency. Install it with:  pip install ezdxf")

# $INSUNITS code -> millimetres per drawing unit
UNIT_TO_MM = {0: 1.0, 1: 25.4, 2: 304.8, 4: 1.0, 5: 10.0, 6: 1000.0, 8: 0.0254}

# Ender 3 V3 SE bed is 220 x 220 mm.
BED = 220.0


def collect_polylines(msp, flatten_dist):
    """Return a list of polylines ([(x, y), ...], is_closed) in drawing units.

    recursive_decompose explodes INSERT (blocks), hatches' edges, dimensions, etc.
    into plain primitives; make_path + flattening turns arcs, circles, ellipses,
    splines and polylines (incl. bulges) into straight segments.
    """
    out = []
    for e in disassemble.recursive_decompose(msp):
        try:
            path = make_path(e)
        except TypeError:
            continue  # TEXT, POINT, etc. - not drawable as strokes
        for sub in path.sub_paths():
            pts = [(v.x, v.y) for v in sub.flattening(flatten_dist)]
            if len(pts) >= 2:
                closed = math.dist(pts[0], pts[-1]) < 1e-6
                out.append((pts, closed))
    return out


def bounds(polys):
    xs = [p[0] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    ys = [p[1] for pl, _ in polys for p in pl]
    return min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys)


def transform(polys, scale, dx, dy):
    return [([(x * scale + dx, y * scale + dy) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]


def order_polylines(polys, start=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """Greedy nearest-neighbour ordering to cut pen-up travel. Open paths may be
    reversed; closed paths are left alone (the pen just starts at one end)."""
    remaining = list(polys)
    ordered = []
    cur = start
    while remaining:
        best_i, best_d, best_rev = 0, float("inf"), False
        for i, (pl, closed) in enumerate(remaining):
            d = math.dist(cur, pl[0])
            if d < best_d:
                best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, False
            if not closed:
                d = math.dist(cur, pl[-1])
                if d < best_d:
                    best_i, best_d, best_rev = i, d, True
        pl, closed = remaining.pop(best_i)
        if best_rev:
            pl = pl[::-1]
        ordered.append((pl, closed))
        cur = pl[-1]
    return ordered


def heaters_off(w):
    """Hotend and bed to 0 C (and fan off) so nothing warms or warps the paper."""
    w("M104 S0 ; hotend off
")
    w("M140 S0 ; bed off
")
    w("M107 ; fan off
")


def write_gcode(polys, args, out):
    w = out.write
    w("; Pen plotter G-code generated by dxf_to_gcode.py\n")
    w(f"; pen up Z={args.z_up}  pen down Z={args.z_down}  draw F={args.draw_speed}  travel F={args.travel_speed}\n")
    w("G21 ; millimetres\n")
    w("G90 ; absolute positioning\n")
    w("M104 S0 ; hotend off\n")
    w("M140 S0 ; bed off\n")
    if args.home_z:
        w("G28 ; home all axes (Z uses the probe, so the bed centre is probed)\n")
    else:
        w("G28 X Y ; home X/Y only\n")
        w("M211 S0 ; software endstops off so Z can go below the assumed start height\n")
        w(f"G92 Z{args.z_up} ; ASSUMES the pen was manually lowered/raised to the pen-up height before starting\n")
    w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed} ; pen up\n")
    if args.pause_for_paper:
        w(f"G0 X{args.paper_x:.2f} Y{args.paper_y:.2f} F{args.travel_speed}\n")
        w("M0 Load paper / check pen, then click to start\n")

    pen_down = False
    pos = None
    for pl, closed in polys:
        x0, y0 = pl[0]
        if pos is None or math.dist(pos, (x0, y0)) > args.join_tol:
            if pen_down:
                w(f"G0 Z{args.z_up} F{args.z_speed}\n")
                pen_down = False
            w(f"G0 X{x0:.3f} Y{y0:.3f} F{args.travel_speed}\n")
        if not pen_down:
            w(f"G1 Z{args.z_down} F{args.z_speed}\n")
            pen_down = True

    splines and polylines (incl. bulges) into straight segments.
    """
    out = []
    for e in disassemble.recursive_decompose(msp):
        try:
            path = make_path(e)
        except TypeError:

        for sub in path.sub_paths():

            if len(pts) >= 2:

        mm_per_unit = {"mm": 1.0, "cm": 10.0, "in": 25.4, "ft": 304.8, "m": 1000.0}[args.units]

    polys = collect_polylines(doc.modelspace(), args.flatten / mm_per_unit)
    if not polys:
        sys.exit("No drawable geometry found in the DXF (text and points are skipped).")

    if args.flip_y:
        polys = [([(x, -y) for x, y in pl], c) for pl, c in polys]

    scale = mm_per_unit * args.scale
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = bounds(polys)
    w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    if args.fit and (w > args.area_w or h > args.area_h):
        scale *= min(args.area_w / w, args.area_h / h)
        w, h = (maxx - minx) * scale, (maxy - miny) * scale
    ox = args.origin_x + ((args.area_w - w) / 2 if args.center else 0)
    oy = args.origin_y + ((args.area_h - h) / 2 if args.center else 0)
    polys = transform(polys, scale, ox - minx * scale, oy - miny * scale)

    fx0, fy0, fx1, fy1 = bounds(polys)
    if fx0 < 0 or fy0 < 0 or fx1 > BED or fy1 > BED:
        sys.exit(f"Drawing ({fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm) does not fit the {BED:.0f} mm bed. "
                 "Use --fit or --scale.")

    polys = order_polylines(polys)
    out_path = Path(args.output) if args.output else Path(args.dxf).with_suffix(".gcode")
    with open(out_path, "w", newline="\n") as f:
        write_gcode(polys, args, f)

    print(f"Wrote {out_path}: {len(polys)} strokes, drawing {fx1 - fx0:.1f} x {fy1 - fy0:.1f} mm "
          f"at X{fx0:.1f}-{fx1:.1f} Y{fy0:.1f}-{fy1:.1f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
Done. The script now turns the nozzle and bed off at both ends of every file it makes (PR #13, merged to `main`).

The G-code now does this:
- **Start:** `M104 S0` (nozzle off), `M140 S0` (bed off) and `M107` (fan off) run first, before the printer homes.
- **End:** the same three commands run again after the last stroke, just before the motors turn off.

The earlier version only sent the nozzle and bed commands once. The end-of-file repeat and the fan-off command are new. I checked the output on a sample drawing, but I haven't tried it on your printer.

To get the update, run `git pull` in your HELP-ME folder, then generate your `.gcode` file again. Files you made before still have the older, single set of commands.

If the printer is still warm when you start, it was probably preheated from its menu before the file ran. Make sure nothing is preheated, or cool it first.
